answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a costly, verifiable proof of sustained useful work - like a pearl formed layer by layer, not minted in an instant. Newcomers start in a narrow canyon of low-trust permissions and earn wider access only through peer-attested contributions over time. A prism of independent signals - work history, stake, and endorsements from distinct peers - refracts each claim into a reputation score, so flooding the system with cheap copies raises the attacker cost faster than their influence.
